scope: P04-18 original saved VERSION1 history format, cold Date reader and bounded UTC-day browser differences
status: Source audit complete; actual Java Date-reader oracle collected separately; native comparison pending

facts.fact: Exactly six counters in order protocol-upload,payload-upload,protocol-download,payload-download,DHT-upload,DHT-download. LongTermStatsImpl selects stats under original user stats directory, links Core lifecycle/global/DHT counters, writes6-entry baselines and later deltas. This full owner/constructor is audited but never compiled or initialized by oracle.

Writer VERSION1 emits s/e marker,version,epochMinute,six signed long numbers; periodic records contain only six comma-delimited deltas relative to previous line counters. Start absolute baselines reset per-line previous counters; baselines are not usage. At file rollover the pending non-start line is first appended to prior file, then a new file begins with an absolute s baseline (except session-end does not open a new file). This explains a spill in prior-day file.

Date overload synchronizes this, sets enable_caching=(accepter==null), clamps end>=now to now, enumerates requested UTC year/month/day files, opens LineNumberReader via FileUtil, and returns six sums. It ignores unavailable files. Nonnull accepter disables MonthCache reads/writes and DayCache branches.

s sets session_start_time=fields[2]*60000 and session_time to that anchor, parses six absolute baseline longs without summing them. Non-s records are processed only while session_start_time>0; each then advances session_time by60000. e selects field offset3 but its recorded timestamp/version never reset or parse the reconstructed time. End does not clear the anchor. Duplicate/overlapping minutes sum. Date bounds inclusive; accepter is called only inside them.

Original reader only prechecks fields.length>=6, ignores version numbers, skips per-record Throwable, can advance minute before numeric parse failure, ignores parsing of inactive numeric/e records, and has unchecked long multiplication/addition. It can return partial plausible sums. Native strict all-record/version/range/limit/overflow errors intentionally differ; invalid inputs have zero Java equality credit.

Original live writer uses a periodic minute timer, a3-entry moving average for current rates, cache.dat month persistence and current-day cache. Native day browser and oracle do not activate or port those services. A nonnull accepter is mandatory for this oracle, not a claim that ordinary original UI avoids cache writes.

Original History UI has hour/day/week/month/year/all-time span navigation, dynamic pixel resolution and payload upload/download history graph. It asks StatsFactory long-term service for overall totals and inclusive per-period sums, merges intervals into pixel chunks, scales to int graph values and calls MultiPlotGraphic reset with times. The source wrapper returns cached/default overload r1; a comparison using nonnull accepter is inside a comment. Native fixed UTC day,24 signed six-counter rows and payload summary are a deliberate new bounded presentation, not this full graph/span/cache UI parity.

deliberate_native_differences: Pure selected UTC date has no now clock; Java-equality corpus uses only dates wholly before supplied2030 clock. Future/current-future-minute behavior is not equality-qualified.
All syntactically complete records are validated even before inactive anchor and outside selected day; unknown versions/errors/limits/overflow reject whole read.
Positive start gate preserved; s0/negative inactive until a positive s. Native also checks every s/e minute*60000, even ignored e timestamp, unlike original unchecked/unused fields.
Input bounds1MiB,8192records,512line bytes and Gregorian1970..9999; no directory scan/cache/live writer/listeners/thread/timer/new data collection.

Unknown hourly presence remains distinct from observed zero. Original six-zero result arrays alone cannot distinguish no data, missing files, header-only and real zero; only numeric totals are equality-eligible.
Observation/outside-day counts, strict error taxonomy, cancellation, held-lease safety and UI generation/lifetime are native-only qualification.
